title: Update READMEs for streaming + structured output quickstarts (copy/paste correctness)
author: Jean-Paul Laurent
release_notes: Quickstarts READMEs now use the canonical streaming + structured output patterns and include explicit env var/model setup so that copy/paste works end-to-end across Node/Python/Go.
description:
Summary: This PR updates quickstart READMEs to be copy/paste correct for the refreshed streaming + structured output examples. The primary issues we saw in smoke tests and support reports were (a) missing/unclear env vars, (b) model name mismatches between code and README, (c) expected output not matching streaming assembly behavior, and (d) JSON parsing guidance that didn’t match schema-constrained output realities. Changes are documentation-only (no runtime template logic changes) but align the READMEs with the current recommended interface semantics and the updated SDK snippets.

What changed (high level): 1) Standardized environment variable instructions across templates, including an explicit “minimum required” set and optional overrides: REDWOOD_API_KEY (required), REDWOOD_BASE_URL (optional; defaults to hosted), REDWOOD_MODEL (required for chat/generation templates), REDWOOD_EMBEDDINGS_MODEL (optional; only for embedding templates), and REDWOOD_TIMEOUT_S (optional). 2) Model selection guidance is now explicit and consistent with the code: each template README includes a “Recommended models” section and a “Known differences by model family” callout (structured output strictness + tool calling variance). 3) Streaming READMEs now show the canonical assembly behavior: print partial deltas to stdout for user feedback, but only treat the final message as authoritative for parsing/validation. Added an expected console transcript that distinguishes delta lines from the final assembled message. 4) Structured output READMEs now include schema-first guidance (with a JSON schema snippet), a validation step, and a safe retry/fallback suggestion when validation fails (including the note that you should not attempt to parse incomplete JSON mid-stream). 5) Standardized prerequisites: Node >= 18, Python >= 3.10, Go >= 1.22; plus a single “Verify credentials” step for each language that fails fast with a helpful error message.

Templates impacted: - agentic-workflow (Node/Python/Go): clarified required env vars, pinned example model names, added expected output sections for tool-result loop completion and final structured response. - streaming-chat (Node/Python/Go): fixed README to match the new streaming event handling (delta vs final), added a short troubleshooting section for disconnect/retry semantics. - structured-output-json-schema (Node/Python/Go): added schema snippet, validation instructions, and an explicit note about model support variability.

Why: This is part of the broader streaming/tool calling/structured output examples refresh. The README is the first place PLG users hit; when the steps aren’t copy/paste correct, we get avoidable support volume and users bounce before first success. This PR is specifically focused on “docs correctness” and minimizing footguns without introducing new SDK APIs.

Notes for reviewers: - Please sanity-check that the model names referenced in each README match what’s in the template code and that the expected output is consistent with the canonical streaming conventions (delta events are illustrative; final message is authoritative). - The structured-output guidance intentionally avoids implying a hard guarantee of valid JSON for all models; we show validation + retry as best practice.

Follow-ups (not in this PR): - Add a small CI smoke test that runs the README commands in a sandboxed environment (blocked on secrets handling). - After merge, update the docs site quickstart links to point to the refreshed templates (tracked in ENG-4826).
commits: docs(quickstarts): standardize env var setup + prerequisites across templates
docs(streaming): align expected output with delta vs final assembly behavior
docs(structured-output): add JSON schema snippet + validation + retry guidance
docs: add troubleshooting section for common streaming/JSON pitfalls
conversation: Wei Chen (review): The env var block still implies REDWOOD_MODEL is optional in the streaming template. Can we make it required and show a concrete model string so the first run works? Also please add a note about not parsing partial JSON mid-stream (ties to SUP-18436).

Jean-Paul Laurent (author): Updated all streaming READMEs to require REDWOOD_MODEL and added a concrete example. Added the “don’t parse partial JSON” note + validation-first guidance in the structured output template.

Dana Lo (review): Node instructions should specify Node 18+ (we’ve seen users on 16 with fetch issues). Also the expected output shows a single line; streaming prints multiple deltas now. Suggest distinguishing “delta output” vs “final assembled message”.
Jean-Paul Laurent (author): Done. Node >= 18 added across templates. Expected output updated to show (1) delta lines and (2) the final assembled content block.
Mateusz Zielinski (review): Go README: the command uses `go run .` but the module is nested; needs `go run ./cmd/app` (or update layout). Please make command match repo layout so it actually works.
Jean-Paul Laurent (author): Fixed the Go commands to match current template layout and verified locally with Go 1.22.
Leila Farouk (review): Suggest adding a minimal “Verify credentials” step so users fail fast on missing key instead of getting a confusing 401 after they’ve installed deps.
Jean-Paul Laurent (author): Added a short “Verify credentials” step + common error messages section (401/403, missing model, invalid JSON).
Elliot Price (approve): Reads well and matches the canonical guidance. Thanks for keeping it honest about model variability while still giving an end-to-end path that works.
ci_summary: Checks: lint-markdown (pass), link-check (pass), spellcheck (pass), template-smoke (pass). One transient link-check failure on first run due to upstream docs redirect; re-run passed after cache refresh.
